why: Asks where the OSI/TCP-IP application layer is implemented (end system vs NIC vs Ethernet). This is general data communications / OSI layering, not web architecture; no TECH1 or TECH2 leaf covers the OSI stack.
Header encapsulation/decapsulation as a packet moves up the OSI layers. Pure data communications and networking, which the 2026 syllabus does not contain.
Properties of the OSI reference model (layer independence, duplicated functionality). General networking theory; no leaf in either paper covers the OSI model.
Addressing levels in TCP/IP — physical vs logical vs port vs specific address. This is data communications addressing, not OS process management and not web architecture.
Function of the OSI physical layer (bit-by-bit delivery). Data communications; outside the 2026 syllabus.
Mechanical and electrical specifications provided by the physical layer, i.e. connectors, cables and signal levels. Transmission media / data communications, explicitly outside the current syllabus.
Relationship between the physical layer and the layer above it in the OSI stack. General networking layering, not covered by any TECH1 or TECH2 unit.
Wireless transmission media — radio, microwave, infrared. Transmission media is data communications and has no leaf in the 2026 syllabus.
LLC vs MAC sublayers of the data link layer. Data communications / LAN standards; not web architecture and not in any unit of either paper.

Hamming distance between identical code words — error detection and coding theory. The Discrete Mathematics unit covers sets, logic, combinatorics, graphs, automata and fuzzy sets, none of which reach coding theory.
Software process models (Build & Fix, Prototyping, Evolutionary, Waterfall) and their ability to absorb change. Software engineering, which the 2026 syllabus dropped entirely.
Choosing a software life cycle model based on team experience. Software engineering / process models; no unit of TECH1 or TECH2 covers SDLC.
Internal vs external software quality attributes. Software quality assurance, part of software engineering and outside the current syllabus.
Classifying a quality requirement as developer-facing (testability) versus user-facing. Software requirements engineering / quality attributes — software engineering.
Definition of coupling as a module's degree of interconnection. Cohesion and coupling are software design metrics; the 2026 syllabus contains no software engineering unit.
Size-oriented software metrics based on lines of code. Software measurement and project management — software engineering.
Risk categories in software project management (product vs project vs business risk). Software engineering; not covered by either paper.
Granularity levels of software testing and which one exercises module cooperation. Software testing, part of software engineering and outside the syllabus.
Risk exposure formula RE = P * L from software risk management. Software project management — software engineering, dropped from the 2026 syllabus.
Characteristics of a good SRS (verifiable, traceable, modifiable, complete). Requirements engineering — software engineering, not present in TECH1 or TECH2.
